paper.title: No Regret Bound for Extreme Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Extreme bandit setting (max K-armed bandit), minimization of the single smallest cost (lower bound)
unmapped: Extreme bandit objective: minimize the expected minimum cost min_{t<=T} x_{k_t,t} observed over the horizon (not the cumulative cost)

Performance measured by 'extreme regret' R_T = (1/T) min{T' : E[min_{t<=T'} x_{k_t,t}] <= E[min_{t<=T} x_{k*_t,t}]}, a ratio of horizons, against the single-armed oracle that plays argmin_k E[min_{t<=T} x_{k,t}]
settings.definition_quote: We are given a tuple of unknown distributions (arms)~$\mu_1^K=(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_K)$. The~$k$th distribution generates sample~$x_{k,t}$ at time~$t$ ... We define the extreme regret of the policy $\pi$ with respect to the oracle policy $\pi_*$ over a time horizon of $T$ as R_T^{\pi,\pi_*} = \frac{1}{T} \min_{T' \ge 1} \{ T' : E[ \min_{t \le T'} x_{k_t,t} ] \le E[ \min_{t \le T} x_{k_t^*,t} ] \}.

conditions: comparator is the single-armed oracle playing argmin_k E[min_{t<=T} x_{k,t}] (also holds against the optimal oracle)
quantity is the extreme regret R_T (ratio of horizons) of Definition 4
hard instances are mixtures of point masses on [0,1] at values alpha_i=(8K)^{-(i!)^2}

source.label: thm:main_result
source.quote: For any policy~$\pi$, there exist distributions $\mu_1^K$ such that $\limsup_T R_T^{\pi,\pi_*} \ge K$, where $\pi_*$ is the single-armed oracle.

results.notes: Extreme regret is a horizon ratio, not additive regret; quantity set to other. Objective mapping to other_pure_exploration is approximate (extreme bandit objective not in vocabulary). Shows no policy achieves 'no extreme regret' (limsup R_T <= 1).
